descriptions: BBSRC provides strategic funding to eight independent UK research institutes. Control of Infectious Diseases: In low- and middle-income countries livestock are often vital to alleviating poverty and hunger, and infections in these animals threaten livelihoods. As such, aspects of this programme remain ODA eligible. These aspects include, breeding for tuberculosis resistant cattle; genome editing to prevent bird flu; role for migratory birds in the global spread of influenza.
Enhanced host repsonses for disease control:  Components of this programme includes research leading to eradication of goat plague (PPR endemic in Asia, Middle East and Africa).
Improving animal production and welfare: this programme includes research uncovering the mechanisms of drug resistance in African livestock trypanosomes, transmitted by tsetse flies.
Understanding and preventing viral diseases: includes resarch on African Swine Fever (Africa), Rift Valley Fever (Africa) and avian influenza (SE Asia) endemic only in LMICs.
Designing Future Wheat: aspects of this programme include improved wheat production systems to pathogens and pests andwheat with enhanced fibre, iron and zinc content.  Research continues on traits for LMIC conditions and resistance to biotic stress local in LMICs.
Soil to nutrition (optimising nutrient flow): includes water use and pest management in LMICs.
